decision.name: CROSS_PROCESS_ARCHIVE_PARTIAL_RECORD_VISIBILITY_ACCEPTANCE
decision.finding: At pinned storage.py, append_observations performs an unsynchronized read/check/append and writes each JSONL record with two separate handle.write calls (body then newline). Besides duplicate-ID races, a partial row becoming visible to a second process before newline can make load_observations raise ValueError. This is a source-derived fault-injection risk, NOT an observed production incident. The new HEAD only improves one-file atomic handoff test hygiene; it does not close archive writer/reader acceptance.

cases: Use multiprocessing.get_context('spawn'), top-level worker entrypoints, tmp_path/observations.jsonl, deterministic valid FlowObservation fixtures; bound all joins/events, terminate stragglers and propagate child errors/exit codes.

Same-ID two-process case: in each child instrument storage.load_observations to synchronize immediately after the initial empty read using a bounded shared Barrier; tolerate BrokenBarrierError when legitimate cross-process serialization prevents both reads concurrently. Require exactly one valid JSONL row and one unique observation_id.
Distinct-ID and distinct revision/economic identity control: require exactly two complete valid JSONL rows, no lost update or malformed/interleaved line.

NEW partial-record visibility case: in writer A only, wrap exact archive append handle so the first body write is flushed to disk and A is event-paused before its newline write; start reader/writer B only after parent receives body-flushed event. Release A in finally after bounded observation; require B not to fail reading partial JSONL and both rows to persist validly. This is controlled fault injection, not a claim of normal buffering behavior; a valid cross-process lock must protect reader from the partial window.

Keep corrected lock-aware two-writer generation test as producer diagnostic; single handoff artifact consumer contract is separate. Do not misclassify three-file coherence as a deployed-reader requirement.
